diagnosis: Candidate/bad runs overrepresent repeated actions: 1,485 repeated operations versus 224 in base/good runs. Repetition comprises 20.2% of bad operations but only 5.9% of good operations (3.40×), especially repeated clicks, no-ops, and scrolling.
expected_mechanism: Detecting unchanged outcomes and forcing a strategy change interrupts unproductive loops, improving task progress and reducing wasted actions. The cost is state comparison, retry bookkeeping, and occasional premature abandonment of a retry that might eventually succeed.
policy_text: Track each action’s observable outcome. If the same or materially equivalent action produces no state change twice, do not repeat it unchanged: inspect the state, alter the target or strategy, or stop that branch. Permit another retry only when new evidence makes success more likely.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -s 'def stats: {operations:(map(.value)|add), tuples:length, sessions:(map(.labels.source_session[0])|unique|length)}; {repeated_bad:(map(select(.stack_frames[0]=="result:repeated" and .value>0))|stats), repeated_good:(map(select(.stack_frames[0]=="result:repeated" and .value<0)|.value=-.value)|stats), all_bad:(map(select(.value>0))|stats), all_good:(map(select(.value<0)|.value=-.value)|stats)}' samples.jsonl
quantitative_evidence.finding: Repeated operations: bad=1,485 across 88 sessions; good=224 across 20 sessions. All operations: bad=7,366; good=3,780. Thus repeated-operation shares are 20.16% and 5.93%, respectively, a 3.40× relative overrepresentation.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(.stack_frames[0]=="result:repeated") | [.stack_frames[2],.value] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{if($2>0)p[$1]+=$2; else n[$1]-=$2} END {for(k in p) printf "%s\tbad=%d\tgood=%d\texcess=%d\n",k,p[k],n[k],p[k]-n[k]}' | sort -t= -k4,4nr
quantitative_evidence.finding: Largest repeated-action excesses were click: 679 bad versus 40 good (+639); noop: 441 versus 85 (+356); and scroll: 278 versus 1 (+277).
